name: Approval Gate
summary: Require explicit, informed user consent before an agent executes a consequential action, with an accurate preview of exactly what will run.
problem: Agents propose actions with real side effects: sending email, deleting records, spending money. Executing without explicit consent destroys trust and can cause irreversible harm, while over-prompting for trivial actions trains users to approve reflexively, which is consent in name only.
useWhen: An agent action has side effects outside the conversation: messages sent, data changed, money spent
The action is irreversible or expensive to reverse
Accountability requires a human decision on record before execution
dontUseWhen: The action is trivially reversible and low-stakes, where gating adds fatigue without safety
The user has durably delegated this action class and revocation is available elsewhere
Read-only operations with no side effects are involved

anatomy.description: Plain-language description of exactly what will happen: the verb, the target, the scope.
Expandable view of the full payload — the actual email text, the command, the diff — so consent is informed.
The control that authorizes execution; labeled with the action, not a generic OK.
The control that declines execution and returns control to the user.
Indicator of reversibility and scope, e.g. 'Cannot be undone' or 'Affects 14 records'.

states.description: The action awaits a decision; nothing has executed.
The user authorized the action; execution may begin.
The action executed successfully; the outcome is reported.
Execution failed after approval; the failure and any partial effects are reported.
The user declined; the action is discarded and nothing executed.
The proposal lapsed without a decision; executing now requires fresh review.

constraints.statement: The proposed action MUST NOT execute without an explicit, affirmative activation of the approve control — never on timeout, scroll, or focus.
constraints.rationale: Anything that executes without a deliberate user gesture is not consent, and one silent execution destroys trust in every future proposal.
constraints.verification: Unit test: no code path reaches the approve callback except activation of the approve control; timers and lifecycle events do not.

constraints.statement: The action summary and detail MUST describe the exact action that will execute, including target, scope, and payload.
constraints.rationale: Consent to a vague summary is not informed consent; if the executed payload differs from the preview, the gate is theater.
constraints.verification: Integration test: the payload rendered in the detail region is byte-identical to the payload passed to execution.

constraints.statement: The approve control MUST NOT receive focus automatically when the gate appears.
constraints.rationale: Auto-focused approve buttons convert muscle-memory Enter presses into authorization of consequential actions.
constraints.verification: Unit test: document.activeElement is unchanged immediately after the gate renders.

constraints.statement: Actions that cannot be undone MUST be labeled as irreversible within the action summary.
constraints.rationale: Reversibility is the single largest input to the approval decision; omitting it makes the risk invisible exactly when it matters.
constraints.verification: Unit test: the irreversible flag renders a visible 'cannot be undone' label inside the summary group.

constraints.statement: Approve and reject MUST be keyboard-operable controls with accessible names that distinguish approval from rejection and name the action.
constraints.rationale: A screen reader user hearing 'button, OK' cannot tell what they are authorizing; the accessible name must carry the decision.
constraints.verification: Axe check plus unit test: both controls are native buttons (or equivalent role) with names like 'Approve: send email' and 'Reject'.

constraints.statement: The arrival of a pending approval MUST be announced to assistive technology.
constraints.rationale: A gate that appears silently leaves screen reader users with a stalled agent and no explanation of what it is waiting for.
constraints.verification: Unit test: a live region announces the pending proposal when the gate mounts.

constraints.statement: Repeated, similar low-risk proposals SHOULD be batchable or groupable so users are not trained to approve reflexively.
constraints.rationale: Approval fatigue is the failure mode of consent: after twenty identical prompts, users stop reading and the gate stops protecting.
constraints.verification: Design review: flows generating many similar proposals offer a batch decision or scoped delegation.

constraints.statement: Proposals MAY expire after inactivity; an expired proposal requires fresh review before execution.
constraints.rationale: Stale proposals can describe a world that no longer exists; expiry forces re-validation of the preview against current state.
constraints.verification: Unit test: an expired proposal cannot be approved without re-issuing it.

wcagCriteria.name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
wcagCriteria.relevance: Consequential submissions must be reviewable, confirmable, and reversible — the approval gate is the mechanism.

wcagCriteria.name: Keyboard
wcagCriteria.relevance: Both decision controls must be fully operable without a pointer.

wcagCriteria.name: Name, Role, Value
wcagCriteria.relevance: Decision controls must expose accessible names that carry the action being authorized.

keyboard.action: Moves through summary, detail disclosure, reject, then approve; reject precedes approve in document order.
Activates the focused control only; no global Enter-to-approve.
Rejects the proposal while focus is inside the gate.

screenReader.behavior: Announcement that an action awaits approval, including the action summary.
Announcement of the outcome: approved and executing, rejected, completed, or failed.

accessibility.focusManagement: Focus is not stolen on appearance and never lands on approve by default; if rendered as a blocking modal, focus moves to the gate container and returns to the trigger on dismissal.
accessibility.reducedMotion: No pulsing or shaking attention effects under prefers-reduced-motion; use static visual emphasis.

do: Name the action in the approve button: 'Approve: send 3 emails', not 'OK'.
Show mutations as diffs in the detail region so before and after are explicit.
Scope each gate to one action; a single approval for a bundle of unlike actions is not informed consent.
dont: Do not auto-approve on a countdown; a timer is not a decision.
Do not bury the payload behind multiple clicks; one disclosure at most.
Do not reuse generic OK/Cancel labels that hide what is being authorized.

references.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding 3.3.4: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Dialog (Modal) pattern
